summary_1line: Bhishma praises the Ajagara vow of effortless acceptance, then begins a tale where Indra (as a jackal) counsels the despairing Brahmin Kasyapa on valuing human life and wisdom.

image_candidates.scene_text: An ascetic calmly sits on bare ground in ragged cloth while rich food and luxurious beds appear and disappear around him, untouched by desire.
A wounded young Brahmin lies on the road beside an overturned chariot as a jackal—Indra in disguise—approaches to speak with him.
The jackal looks at a thorn lodged in its body while insects bite it, lamenting that it lacks hands like humans to remove the pain.
